title: Power Apps: Dataverse custom APIs in generative pages
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft's documentation supports the custom API behaviour, security qualifications, licensing prerequisites and admin paths. The rollout sentence should explicitly describe December 2026 as a roadmap target rather than a settled availability date.

claims.quote: "targetDate": "December CY2026"; "status": "In development"
claims.fix: Replace the rollout sentence with: 'The roadmap targets preview for October CY2026 and general availability for December CY2026 (generative page version 307), in model-driven apps in Worldwide, GCC and GCC High.'

claims.claim: Licensing specific to custom API calls from generative pages, beyond the stated platform premium use rights, is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative pages" "custom API" licensing credits cost. Opened generative-pages, powerapps-licensing-faq and api-request-limits-allocations; read returned licensing excerpts. Premium app requirements are stated; no separate generative-page custom API licensing rule was found.

claims.claim: All Power Apps API requests to Dataverse count as Power Platform requests.
claims.quote: What is a Microsoft Power Platform request? ... **Power Apps**: All API requests to connectors and Microsoft Dataverse.

claims.claim: In-browser authoring requires an environment in the United States, Great Britain, Australia or Singapore.
claims.quote: The Power Platform environment must be located in one of the following regions: United States, Great Britain, Australia, or Singapore.

claims.claim: AI code generation tool authoring is available more widely on public clouds than in-browser authoring.
claims.quote: If your region isn't listed, you can still create and edit generative pages using AI code generation tools, which are available worldwide on public clouds.

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center tenant control is reached through Settings > Tenant settings > Copilot in Power Apps (preview).
claims.quote:
In the navigation pane, select **Settings** to open the **Tenant settings** page.
3. Select **Copilot in Power Apps (preview)**, and then set the toggle to **Off**.

claims.where: controls[0].governs, scope and note; Governance controls: first row
claims.claim: This tenant control governs Copilot preview features for makers.
claims.quote: Turning off Copilot for your tenant turns off Copilot for makers only.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that this general Copilot control disables custom API use in generative pages or calls from published pages.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative pages" "custom API" "disable"; "generative pages" "custom API" "admin" "setting" PowerShell. Opened generative-pages, ai-overview and tenant-settings. No passage links the general maker toggle to this custom API capability or published-page calls.

claims.claim: Tenant settings can also be reached in the Power Platform admin center through Manage > Tenant settings.
claims.quote:
In the navigation pane, select **Manage**.
3. In the **Manage** pane, select **Tenant settings**.

claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for the Copilot in Power Apps preview tenant toggle is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps Copilot preview tenant setting PowerShell Set-TenantSettings Power Platform API. Opened Set-TenantSettings and list-tenantsettings; searched pac admin. No documented property matches this toggle; intelligence.disableCopilot describes canvas how-to answers instead.

claims.claim: Application Insights export setup starts at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Data export > App Insights > New data export.
claims.quote:
In the navigation pane, select **Manage**.
3. In the **Manage** pane, select **Data export**.
4. On the **Data export** page, select the **App Insights** tab. Then select **New data export**.

claims.where: controls[1].governs and scope; Governance controls: second row
claims.claim: Environment-level Application Insights export applies to generative page telemetry.
claims.quote: When you configure Application Insights data export for the environment in the Power Platform admin center, Power Apps automatically exports telemetry for published generative pages.

claims.claim: Application Insights telemetry for generative pages is in preview.
claims.quote: Application Insights telemetry for generative pages is a preview feature. Availability might vary by environment while the feature is rolling out.

claims.claim: Application Insights data export is supported only for Managed Environments.
claims.quote: This feature is turned on and supported for managed environments only.

claims.claim: Export configuration requires the Power Platform administrator or Dynamics 365 administrator role at tenant level.
claims.quote: This includes being assigned to the Power Platform administrator or Dynamics 365 administrator role at the tenant-level in Microsoft Entra ID

claims.claim: The export administrator also needs the environment administrator or system administrator role within the Dataverse environment.
claims.quote: **and** by being assigned to the environment administrator or system administrator role within the Dataverse environment. Without these permissions, the integration doesn't work.

claims.claim: Export setup also requires Contributor or Owner access to the intended Azure Application Insights resource.
claims.quote: Confirm that you have **Contributor** or **Owner** access to the Azure Application Insights resource you intend to use.

claims.claim: An automation equivalent for configuring Power Platform Application Insights data export is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Platform Application Insights data export automation API PowerShell CLI export package; "Application Insights" "export" "Power Platform API". Opened export setup and searched pac admin. Results document UI setup, not an equivalent export-configuration call.

claims.where: controls[2].ui and controls[2].api; Governance controls: third row; Open questions
claims.claim: No dedicated admin UI or automation switch for custom API use in generative pages is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "generative pages" "custom API" "disable"; "generative pages" "custom API" "admin" "setting" PowerShell. Opened generative-pages, tenant-settings, list-tenantsettings and Set-TenantSettings; searched pac admin. No feature-specific switch was found.

claims.claim: Custom API use in a generative page is maker opt-in, represented as user-opt-in.
claims.quote: In the generative page designer, select **Add** > **Custom API**. Searched: "generative pages" "custom API" "disable"; opened feature and tenant settings references. No dedicated admin enablement switch was found.

claims.claim: Dataverse plug-in code can run in another user's context.
claims.quote: Sometimes you need the code in a plug-in to run in the context of a different user, for example to perform an operation on their behalf. There are two ways to apply impersonation in plug-ins: at registration or execution.
